title: Peter Duncan's Jack And The Beanstalk - review
transcript: welcome to one minute theater reviews i'm paul seven lewis and i'm reviewing jack and the beanstalk written by and starring peter duncan which is playing at cinemas all over the uk this christmas as well as streaming online people of a certain age will know peter duncan as a legendary blue peter presenter but he's also a theater person through and through and among his many achievements he's a writer and producer of pantomimes and his are not the kind that use spectacle and star names as a substitute for substance now he puts on traditional pantomimes and realizing that many families would miss the enjoyment of pantomime this year not to mention that many people would be deprived of working on one he decided to film jack and the beanstalk you won't see a better traditional pantomime than this anywhere peter duncan just knows how pantomime works the timing and the pace are excellent and he's really pulled out all the stops um there's everything you'd expect of a traditional pantomime um there's a motherly uh good fairy played by nicola blackman fighting the creepy evil uh played with relish by uh joss van tyler there's a custard pisces a pantomime cow older new jokes and a convincing romance between a heroic jack played by sam ebenezer and jill played by sarah moss and there's an impressive giant there's also very good dancing and tuneful songs in fact the songs are terrific with some clever lyrics one's a great comic sing-along and then there's more of a stirring sort of anthem-like song as jack climbs the beanstalk peter duncan himself plays dame trot and he's a a classic dame with a glorious collection of frocks and wigs and hats the jack and the beanstalk story is followed faithfully but there are topical references cracks about the pandemic and a save the planet to take on the story one bold decision is to not include an audience either a live one or a canned one um what they do instead is leave gaps for the traditional uh responses of you know oh no it isn't and he's behind you um and i think this will work because you really do want to join in the show is filmed in a beautiful garden um which has lots of little nooks and crannies and adds a real enchantment to the story which is after all about climbing a giant plant and although it's filmed outside the sound is very clear and the the filming and editing are all top quality if you want to take your children to enjoy a traditional pantomime with an audience then i think seeing peter duncan's jack and the beanstalk at the cinema would be perfect and i also think it'd be great to gather the whole family round the telly to enjoy this entertainment i give peter duncan's jack and the beanstalk five stars please subscribe to my youtube channel one minute theater reviews you can also read my blog at oneminutetheatreviews.com uk and listen to my stage musicals podcast on boxofficeradio.cod.uk and at mixcloud.com you
